items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: when he was with Jay McShann, later, in the 40s, Charlie Parker was in that band. So Clyde Bernhardt represents almost a microcosm in the history of jazz, having played with King Oliver and Charlie Parker.

ctx.x: But your band has been more about Ellington than —

Well basically what the band is I don’t tell anybody how to play, but if I hear that they’ve got a blues inflection to their playing well that interests me and also, depending on I mean when I had access to the musicians who had done the recordings that I had collected, so I went after some of them, especially if they had any connection to King Oliver. Clyde had some blues with King Oliver and played with him in the 30s. In fact Clyde Bernhardt is rather interesting because when he was with Jay McShann, later, in…
Now your average age has gone up since then, is that right or not?
